definition: An error that makes repeated readings scatter unpredictably above and below the true value; its effect is reduced by repeating readings and taking the mean.
An error that shifts every reading in the same direction, such as a zero error or an uncalibrated instrument; repeating readings does not reduce it.
How close repeated measurements of the same quantity are to each other; random errors reduce it.
How close a measurement, or the mean of several, is to the true value; systematic errors reduce it.
The range above and below a measured value within which the true value is expected to lie, written as value ± uncertainty.
The uncertainty in a quantity given in the quantity's own unit, such as the 0.01 A in (0.34 ± 0.01) A.
The absolute uncertainty divided by the measured value, $\frac{\Delta x}{x}$; it has no unit and is also called the relative uncertainty.
The fractional uncertainty multiplied by 100%, which shows how large the uncertainty is compared with the value.
The size of the difference between an experimental value and the accepted value, divided by the size of the accepted value (ignore any minus sign) and multiplied by 100%.
The change in a quantity divided by its original value and multiplied by 100%; positive for a rise and negative for a fall.
The difference between two values divided by their mean and multiplied by 100%, used to compare two results when neither is an accepted value.
The digits of a number that carry meaning about its precision, counted from the first non-zero digit.
Working out the uncertainty in a calculated result from the uncertainties in the measurements used to calculate it.
